A1.justification: Both complete 28-page PDFs describe RulePlanner with matching sections and Appendices A–O. Text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison; the appendix pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original RulePlanner evaluations on MCNC and GSRC, including baseline comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and transfer experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 3–6 and the additional evaluations in Appendices K–O.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–F retain the same rule matrices, action masking, reward construction, network architecture, and hybrid PPO training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight MCNC/GSRC circuits, three design-constraint tasks, and cross-circuit zero-shot and fine-tuning scenarios. No evaluated dataset or task is added or removed.

E2.justification: The seven main baselines and comparator membership within each appendix comparison are unchanged. EXPlace is newly discussed in Section 6 but is not evaluated against RulePlanner.

E3.justification: Task definitions, metrics, training settings, transfer procedures, and Appendix M's best-of-N inference protocol remain unchanged. Table 6's revised caption does not change the underlying evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The mask ablations in Table 6, runtime analysis in Appendix K, floorplan case study in Figure 8, and threshold-based constraint-adherence analysis in Appendix O are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs with different seeds in Section 5.1 and retain the same plus/minus summaries and shaded learning curves. No uncertainty-reporting practice or run information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Tables 3–4 retain RulePlanner's average block-terminal distance of 0.000 and block-block adjacency length of 0.223.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, formulations, and equations in Sections 2–4 and Appendices B–E are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of unified design-rule handling, novel representations and metrics, extensibility, and transferability. Shortening 'deep reinforcement learning (RL)' to 'RL' in the conclusion does not change its meaning.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretation of constraint compliance versus HPWL, explanation of transferability, and limitation concerning absent thermal optimization. The added related-work discussion introduces no new interpretation or limitation of RulePlanner.

D1.justification: Implementation algorithms, architecture details, software, hardware, hyperparameters, and circuit statistics remain unchanged. Both abstracts retain the same code location and promise of future code availability.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds EXPlace (Gao et al., 2026) and a paragraph covering Bai et al. (2025, 2026) and LaMPlace (Geng et al., 2025). Four references and brief discussion broaden the context to expert-guided placement, logic optimization, circuit generation, and downstream design objectives.

P1.justification: There are limited related-work additions, a shortened phrase in the conclusion, and revised Table 6 wording. Affiliation, correspondence, funding, and publication information are updated; the section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 6's caption is reworded and its emphasis changes. First-page text placement and the conclusion/reference layout reflow, with references beginning on page 9 instead of page 8. Figures, table structures, and appendix layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: Section 6 gives a more complete account of expert-guided placement through EXPlace and connects the work to downstream-aware chip-design research. This modestly improves research context. The method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and stated limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
